# Ridgeway Components Inc. — FY2024 Audit
**Workpaper C-4.2: Test of Operating Effectiveness — Disbursement Approval and Three-Way Match**
Prepared: R. Roe (staff) | Re-performed and completed: Audit Senior | Status: **Control not relied upon — see §5**

---

## 1. Objective

To obtain evidence that, throughout H1 2024, each disbursement was (a) approved by the person authorised for the amount, (b) approved before payment, and (c) three-way matched to PO and receiving report (or validly exempt), with price variances over 5% re-approved — sufficient to reduce substantive testing of expenses and accounts payable.

## 2. Population and sample

| | |
|---|---|
| Population | H1 2024 cash disbursements, 1,240 payments, $8.96m (reconciled to the cash book by Richard; I re-footed) |
| Firm table | TDR 10%, expected deviations 0, required sample **25** |
| Sample drawn | Every 124th payment from a random start = **10 items** |

**Sample adequacy — inadequate.** Interval 124 on a population of 1,240 yields 10 items, not 25; the correct interval was ~49. Ten items with zero deviations would not support reliance at a 10% TDR. However, I have **not extended the sample** (judgement, see §5): re-performance found three deviations in ten items, so even a clean extension to 25 would give an observed rate of 12% with an upper deviation limit well above 10%. Extension would cost time without changing the conclusion.

## 3. Attributes and results (re-performed)

Attributes:
- **A** — Approved at correct level (≤$5k Ops Manager; >$5k–$25k Director; >$25k CFO), assessed on the total commitment, not just the invoice sampled
- **B** — Approval dated before payment date
- **C** — Three-way match to PO and receiving report, variance ≤5% of PO or re-approved; or valid exemption (utility / signed engagement letter)

| # | Vendor | Invoice $ | A | B | C | Comment |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Kestrel Packaging | 4,180.00 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| 2 | Alder Logistics | 12,640.00 | ✓ | ✓ | Δ | Invoice exceeds PO by $640 = **5.3%**. Richard recorded "Yes"; a variance over tolerance needs fresh approval. Director approval 02-12 is at the right level — see §4(d) |
| 3 | Brightwell Chemicals | 24,800.00 | **✗** | ✓ | ✓ | Second invoice BW-7732, $24,600, same day, same product, consecutive PO/invoice numbers. Combined $49,400 → **CFO approval required**; only Director approved |
| 4 | Miles & Roe LLP | 31,500.00 | ✓ | ✓ | EL | CFO approved; PO-exempt under engagement letter (confirm signed copy on file predates service) |
| 5 | Kestrel Packaging | 3,950.00 | ✓ | **✗** | ✓ | Paid 04-10, approved **04-15** — approval five days after payment |
| 6 | Summit IT Services | 18,200.00 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |
| 7 | Cobalt Freight | 7,410.00 | **✗** | ✓ | ✓ | $7,410 > $5,000 → Director required; approved by **Ops Manager** |
| 8 | Northgate Utilities | 2,215.33 | ✓ | ✓ | U | Utility, PO-exempt |
| 9 | Alder Logistics | 11,980.00 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | Variance −0.2%, within tolerance |
| 10 | Pinecrest Tooling | 9,875.00 | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | |

**Tickmark legend:** ✓ attribute met | ✗ deviation | Δ observation, not counted as deviation pending evidence | EL exempt — signed engagement letter | U exempt — utility

**Result: 3 deviations in 10 (30%).** Richard's workpaper identified none.

## 4. Exceptions and root cause

**(a) Item 3 — Brightwell Chemicals: split purchase to avoid CFO approval.** Two POs (4410/4411) and two invoices (BW-7731/7732) for the same coolant concentrate, delivered the same day, each $200–$400 under the $25,000 Director ceiling, both approved by the same Director on 02-27 and paid in the same run. The approval control was applied per invoice and so was circumvented; the authorised approver for a $49,400 purchase never saw it. *Root cause:* threshold is enforced per document rather than per commitment, and there is no detective review for same-vendor/same-day splits. The pattern (consecutive numbers, both just under the limit) is consistent with deliberate structuring and is a **fraud risk indicator** under ISA 240 / AS 2401 — it may be a procurement shortcut, or it may conceal kickbacks or an unapproved supplier arrangement. Not yet discussed with management; to be raised with the CFO (not the Director) by the manager/partner.

**(b) Item 5 — Kestrel Packaging: approval after payment.** Paid 04-10, approved 04-15. *Root cause:* the AP system does not block payment pending approval, so the "approval" is a post-hoc sign-off, not a preventive control. Enquire whether the April 10 run was pushed through for cash-discount or vendor-pressure reasons.

**(c) Item 7 — Cobalt Freight: wrong approval level.** $7,410 approved by Ops Manager; Director required. *Root cause:* the approval matrix is not system-enforced; routing depends on the requester choosing the approver.

**(d) Item 2 — Alder Logistics (observation, open).** 5.3% variance. The Director's 02-12 approval is at the correct level and predates payment, so it satisfies the policy **if** it was an approval of the invoice at $12,640 with the variance visible, rather than a carried-forward PO approval. I have asked AP for the approval record. If it was the PO approval, this becomes a fourth deviation. Either way the conclusion in §5 is unchanged, so I have not held the workpaper for it.

**Other matters.** (i) Item 4 is to a firm named Miles & Roe LLP; I have asked Richard to confirm no relationship — almost certainly coincidental, but documented for independence. (ii) Richard's results table misrecorded three items and the Brightwell ledger was in the file but not read. Review of his other workpapers on this engagement is required; coaching point noted.

## 5. Conclusion and effect on the audit plan

**Conclusion: the control is not operating effectively and cannot be relied upon for H1 2024 (and, absent evidence of remediation, for the year).** Three deviations in ten items exceeds the 10% TDR on any extension. More importantly, the deviations are qualitatively different in kind: one is an apparent circumvention by a Director-level approver, and the other two show the control is not enforced by the system at all.

**Deficiency classification (judgement):** at minimum a **significant deficiency**. Any single Director can commit the company to unlimited amounts by splitting POs, and payments can be made without approval. I would upgrade to a **material weakness** if the full-year analytics (below) show splitting is not isolated to Brightwell, or if the Brightwell matter proves intentional — because that would also impair reliance on management's integrity in the purchasing cycle. To be settled with the manager and partner after the analytics.

**Changes to the plan:**
1. Control risk for purchases/disbursements/AP reset to **high**; expense testing moves to a fully substantive approach. Sample sizes for expense vouching and AP existence/completeness to be recalculated with no controls reliance; search for unrecorded liabilities extended to a lower threshold.
2. Full-year data analytics on all 2024 disbursements: (i) invoices within 10% below each threshold, (ii) multiple POs/invoices to one vendor within 7 days aggregating over a threshold, (iii) approvals dated after payment, (iv) approver vs amount band mismatches. Follow up all hits.
3. Brightwell: examine all 2024 POs, invoices, and receiving reports; identify who raised the POs; compare unit prices to other coolant suppliers; vendor master review (set-up date, bank changes, ownership).
4. Fraud risk assessment updated; the Brightwell split and the plan to address it to be communicated to those charged with governance per ISA 260/265 before year-end fieldwork.
5. Remove any planned reliance on other controls performed by the same Director until the matter is resolved.

## 6. Proposed management letter points

1. **Apply thresholds to the commitment, not the document.** Approval level should be determined by total expected spend per vendor per order; configure the ERP to flag multiple POs to one vendor within a set period that aggregate above a threshold, with CFO review of all items within 10% of a limit.
2. **Make approval preventive.** Block the payment run for any invoice without a completed, timestamped approval; remove the ability to approve after payment.
3. **System-enforce the approval matrix.** Route invoices by amount band automatically; approvers should be unable to approve above their limit.
4. **Price-variance workflow.** Variances over 5% should route for re-approval with the variance displayed, and the re-approval should be recorded against the invoice.
5. **Detective review.** Monthly report to the CFO of disbursements by approver, amount band, and threshold proximity; evidence of review retained.
6. **Brightwell.** Management should investigate the February split, confirm pricing was arm's-length, and reinforce the procurement policy with Directors.
